live.name: ALPHV
live.headline: ALPHV: a ransomware actor known by several names
live.in_short: The catalogue lists ALPHV under several aliases and a set of tools. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: ALPHV is the main name for this actor in the catalogue record.
It is also listed as ALPHVM, Ambitious Scorpius, BlackCat Gang and UNC4466.
The catalogue links the name to tools including BlackCat, Noberus, Munchkin, Mimikatz, Impacket, PsExec, LaZagne, MEGAsync and GO Simple Tunnel (GOST).
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: ALPHV
next.headline: ALPHV (BlackCat): a ransomware-as-a-service gang that hit hospitals, cities and casinos before an apparent exit scam
next.in_short: ALPHV, also called BlackCat, ran a ransomware-for-hire business from late 2021. It stole data, threatened to leak it, and claimed victims in many sectors. In March 2024 BleepingComputer reported it appeared to be exit scamming.

sentences.t: ALPHV is also tracked as ALPHVM, BlackCat Gang, Ambitious Scorpius and UNC4466, according to the ETDA catalogue.
Cybernews reports that the ransomware was first observed in late 2021. It also notes the group's use of the Rust programming language.
The gang ran a ransomware-as-a-service business, selling malware subscriptions to criminals, Cybernews says. Sygnia likewise says BlackCat employs that model.
BleepingComputer says ALPHV is believed to be a rebrand of the DarkSide and BlackMatter ransomware operations. A report on the Alexandria attack says unnamed experts hold the same view.

BleepingComputer reports that the FBI linked the gang to over 60 breaches in its first four months. The FBI also estimates it took at least $300 million in ransom payments from over 1,000 victims until September 2023.
ReliaQuest says the Scattered Spider group has strategic alliances with ALPHV and other ransomware operators. Check Point lists BlackCat/ALPHV among the tools noted for Scattered Spider.

Victims named in the cards span local government and healthcare. They also include finance and software. A report on Alexandria, Louisiana, says the gang had also attacked at least three US colleges and universities that year.

DataBreaches reports that the 2022 attack on Suffolk County disabled its 911 system and other services. The group claimed 400 GB of county and contractor data. DataBreaches could not confirm the leak.

Cybernews reports that the gang listed NJVC, an IT company supporting US government and defense bodies, on its leak site in September 2022. It then removed the listing. The breach is the gang's own claim.

The gang claimed over 1 TB stolen from Constellation Software, a Canadian software group. The company confirmed that some internal systems were breached and that some personal and business partner data was taken.
The gang's core tactic was double extortion. It stole data, listed the victim on a leak site, and threatened to publish the files unless the victim paid or negotiated.

Sygnia investigated a 2023 attack it attributes to BlackCat or one of its affiliates. Entry came through a compromised third-party vendor. The attacker spent weeks moving through the network with Cobalt Strike and tunnelling tools, then copied data to cloud storage with Rclone.

In that case the attacker sent extortion emails to dozens of employees. Sygnia says the client cut off internet access, which stopped the encryption. The files were later posted on the group's leak site.
The catalogue lists tools tied to the group. They include Mimikatz, PsExec, Impacket, LaZagne, MEGAsync and GO Simple Tunnel.

In the Suffolk County case, DataBreaches noted screenshots of the county's Veeam backup tools. A group admin said everything should have been removed. DataBreaches read this as an intent to delete backups, though that is not proof it happened.
CrowdStrike Intelligence reports that in the first quarter of 2023, ransomware-as-a-service platforms including Alphv were used to target VMware ESXi hypervisors.

In its own statement on the September 2023 MGM Resorts attack, AlphV said it launched ransomware against more than 100 ESXi hypervisors. It also said it kept super administrator access to MGM's Okta and other systems. These are the gang's claims, not verified by the article.
Henry Schein disclosed a cybersecurity incident on October 15, 2023. The report says AlphV claimed responsibility and re-encrypted systems after negotiations broke down.
BleepingComputer reports that an international law enforcement operation seized the gang's Tor negotiation and leak sites in December 2023.
In December 2023, DataBreaches reported that AlphV claimed to have pressured a Viking Therapeutics employee into filing an SEC complaint. DataBreaches called the breach unconfirmed.

In early 2024 the gang claimed breaches of loanDepot and Prudential Financial. BleepingComputer notes the claims were unverified at the time. loanDepot later said at least 16.6 million people had data stolen.

BleepingComputer reported that unnamed sources linked the Change Healthcare attack to BlackCat. It could not confirm this, and the gang had not claimed the attack at the time. UnitedHealth's SEC filing described a suspected nation-state actor.

By March 2024, BleepingComputer reported, the gang appeared to be running an exit scam. Its sites went offline, affiliates said they were not paid, and the source code was offered for $5 million. ALPHV told the outlet its infrastructure had been seized, and Europol and the NCA denied involvement. BleepingComputer said it was unclear whether the group would return under a new name.
Keep backups offline and test restores. Limit and monitor third-party vendor access. Prepare a plan for cutting off network access fast.
